decision.detail: I set the reel down on the booth shelf, cap it, tuck it under my arm. The old projectionist is still talking—something about the lamphouse, the way the carbon arc used to spit blue. I don't reach for the camera. I just stand there and let him finish. Nod once. Say, "Yeah. It was louder back then." He grunts, satisfied. I pull my coat on. The ballroom lights are doing their slow amber turn out there, visible through the screen-room window, and they're fine. They don't need me to point a lens at them. The station line is open, Rita's patch is live, my reel is in my bag. I walk out through the lobby, past the ticket booth, out the side door into the February air. I'm done.
decision.intention: One take, one voice, one reel. It's mine. I'm not projecting it, I'm not handing it to anyone, I'm not running it through a ballroom screen. I listened to the old man because he wanted to say a few words and it cost me nothing to hear them. Now I go home. The lights can keep spinning without me.
decision.words: Yeah. It was louder back then.
